nodes.label: Signal — fine-grained reactivity unit
nodes.rationale: A signal bound to a DOM node updates only that node — there is no re-render, no virtual DOM, no component re-run. This is fine-grained reactivity.

nodes.label: Run-once component (setup, not render)
nodes.rationale: The component body runs exactly once on mount (Solid-style, not React); it is setup not render. Consequences: no hook-ordering rules, props that change are passed as signals, and a matched component's state and effects survive parent re-renders.

nodes.label: Computed — derived read-only signal
nodes.rationale: Recomputes only when a listed dependency changes; read-only. Use instead of recomputing in the run-once body.

nodes.label: Declarative control flow (Show/ShowElse/Switch/For/VirtualList)
nodes.rationale: Because the component body runs once, plain if/for cannot react to signal changes; declarative control flow with stable keys re-renders the affected scope while preserving row identity and element state.

nodes.label: Effects with explicit deps (OnMount/Watch/UseEffect)
nodes.rationale: All effects declare dependencies explicitly — there is no auto-tracking. OnMount is client-only (never runs during SSR); cleanup functions run on change/unmount to avoid goroutine leaks.

nodes.label: Off-loop updates via core.Schedule
nodes.rationale: Timers, goroutines, network callbacks and channel receives run outside the render loop and must not set signals directly — that races the renderer. Schedule enqueues the update on the frame queue, drained once per frame.

nodes.label: UseResource — async data loading
nodes.rationale: Returns Data/Loading/Err signals plus Refetch, runs the fetch in a goroutine and applies the result safely. Fetching is client-side, so SSR renders the loading state and the client fills it after hydration.

nodes.label: ErrorBoundary — contains render-time panics
nodes.rationale: Catches a panic while rendering a child and renders a fallback so the rest of the page stays intact; update-time panics keep the subtree's previous state and are logged.

nodes.label: SSR + hydration
nodes.rationale: SSR emits data-node-id attributes and text markers; the client detects the server DOM and hydrates (claims nodes, wires handlers) instead of rebuilding. Hydration trusts server and client to produce identical markup; a structural mismatch logs a console.error and recovers best-effort.

nodes.label: h.Dynamic — hydration escape hatch
nodes.rationale: Wraps a legitimately non-deterministic subtree (dates, locale, per-request data) so the client's value wins over the server's on hydration, keeping the rest of the markup deterministic.

nodes.label: Client-side routing (path-based, History API)
nodes.rationale: Matching is deterministic: exact match wins, then most-specific param/prefix. ParamSignal binds reactively (updates in place, no remount); Param is a one-shot read for handlers.

nodes.label: Refs & portals — imperative DOM / out-of-tree render
nodes.rationale: Refs give imperative DOM access (Focus/Blur/Click/ScrollIntoView) instead of reaching into syscall/js; portals render modals/tooltips outside the current subtree.
nodes.norm_label: refs & portals — imperative dom / out-of-tree render

nodes.label: bridge package — bridge.Run WASM entry point
nodes.rationale: bridge.Run mounts the app, hydrates server-rendered DOM when present, and drives the render loop. It never returns, keeping the WASM module alive to service events — the single client entry point.
nodes.norm_label: bridge package — bridge.run wasm entry point

nodes.label: Metadata container — collected into <head>
nodes.rationale: Wraps head elements anywhere in the tree; renderers collect children and inject into <head>. Head children must be static (Title/Meta/Link/Script/StyleEl/Fragment); reactive head content is not collected into the SSR head.

nodes.label: Page(PageMeta) — full SEO/social/JSON-LD constructor
nodes.rationale: Expands a single config into title, OG/Twitter cards, JSON-LD and LLM meta, propagating each field to every relevant format; returns a Fragment so it composes inside Metadata.

nodes.label: Structured logging via core.Log (recover boundaries)
nodes.rationale: Every recover boundary and reactive warning emits an entry with a stable kind field (recover.event_handler, recover.error_boundary, recover.re_render, signal.cycle, warn); the WASM bridge forwards the payload to goowee.log() which routes to console.error/warn/log by kind.

nodes.label: Dev-mode inspector (goowee.inspect / devtools.Snapshot)
nodes.rationale: Snapshots the mounted component/scope/element tree and registered signals; signals are auto-registered from UseState/UseResource/Computed when devtools are enabled. Enabled via ?goowee-dev or localStorage; bridge.Run enables it when goowee.devEnabled() is true.

nodes.label: Public/internal API boundary
nodes.rationale: core mixes the public reactive API with framework internals; only a named subset (Signal/NewSignal/Computed/SignalAccessor/Schedule/Node/Component/ComponentNode/EventData/Ref/SVGNamespace) is public. The rest stays exported only because renderer packages share it across package boundaries — Go's internal/ visibility is per-package not per-identifier, and splitting core is a larger tracked refactor.

nodes.label: v0 stability policy
nodes.rationale: v0 allows breaking changes between minor releases (called out in CHANGELOG); renames keep the old name for one minor with a // Deprecated pointer. At v1 the public surface freezes under semver.

nodes.label: internal/dom — DOM renderer, diff, hydration, event registry
nodes.rationale: Under internal/ so the Go toolchain prevents any external module from importing it; there is no supported way to drive the renderer directly — go through bridge.Run (client) or ssr (server).
nodes.norm_label: internal/dom — dom renderer, diff, hydration, event registry

nodes.label: runtime/goowee.js — JS bridge (applies mutations, forwards events)
nodes.rationale: Implementation detail of the client, not a stable interface; applies mutations and forwards events, and hosts goowee.boot/log/inspect/devEnabled.
nodes.norm_label: runtime/goowee.js — js bridge (applies mutations, forwards events)

nodes.label: SPA fallback deployment (serve index.html for unmatched paths)
nodes.rationale: The WASM binary reads window.location.pathname at boot via router.CurrentPath(); if the server 404s a deep link the app never bootstraps. Serving index.html for unmatched paths lets the WASM load, read the URL, and render client-side. goowee routing is path-based (History API), not hash-based; a <base href> lets the same binary work at root or a sub-path.
nodes.norm_label: spa fallback deployment (serve index.html for unmatched paths)

nodes.label: WASM compression — the biggest boot-latency lever
nodes.rationale: Download+compile of the ~4MB wasm binary is ~65-75% of time-to-interactive, so serving it compressed (gzip ~3.7x, brotli ~4.2x) is the single biggest boot-latency lever — bigger and far cheaper than shrinking the binary with TinyGo. Compression does not shrink the compiled module or the ~40ms Go runtime boot.
nodes.norm_label: wasm compression — the biggest boot-latency lever
